meta.units: local metres (origin LV95 2681400/1248700), z = world height of platform top incl. terrain z_shift -3.06
sources: SBB Open Data: BehiG Haltekantesegment (data.sbb.ch/explore/dataset/21197_behig-haltekantesegment), Perron nr/type/length, track axis at Haltekante start/end; licence https://data.sbb.ch/page/licence (Open-Data-Lizenz, attribution 'Quelle: SBB')
meta.note: edges[].line = polyline of the TRACK-SIDE platform edge (local m); z_top per vertex = rail head (terrain z + 0.29) + 0.55 m. Track axis = edge shifted 1.67 m away from the platform (SBB P55 standard). For in_osm=true perrons the edge is the OSM polygon side that lies <2.8 m from an OSM rail; for in_osm=false (Altstetten 3/4, 6/7: not mapped in OSM) polygon and edges are derived from the OSM track lines (edge = track -+ 1.67 m) with the official SBB length/position; these perrons' slab, kerb, white line, tactile strip and canopy are built in web/public/models/landmarks/stp_*.glb, so pipeline/railways.py must NOT build them again (keep OSM tracks as they are: official and OSM track positions differ by up to ~3 m, the platforms follow OSM). edges[].track = official track number ('?' = not in the official list).

perrons.polygon_source: derived: SBB BehiG length/position + OSM track lines, edge = axis -+ 1.67 m
